subject: Difference between confmirt() amd mirt() and more

messages.author: f532f98b3e9b7d93
messages.subject: Difference between confmirt() amd mirt() and more
parts:
Hi Phil,

1)Would you please explain what's the difference between confmirt() amd mirt() when there is no specified model for confmirt() and only number of factors is specified?

2) in model building for confmirt(), what does do COV? for example, having two factors like f1 and f2 with 10 items, I know that:
a) f1=1-5 #items related to f1
b) f2= 5-10 #items related to f2 and item5 has cross loading on f1 anf f2

but I'm not sure about these ones:
c) (f1*f2)= 2-7 #items affected by interaction between f1 and f2
d) COV= f1*f2 # freeing covariance between f1 and f2

would you please help me on the above issues?

Thanks,
Amin.

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Difference between confmirt() amd mirt() and more
parts:
Hi Amin,

The only difference between confmirt and mirt is the estimator used,
but syntactically they are exactly the same. mirt uses marginal
maximum likelihood and confmirt uses the MH-RM, and as of the dev
version 0.8.3 they are actually exactly the same syntactically since
polynomial interactions are allowed. I think in the next version I
will actually deprecate the confmirt function just add a method =
'MHRM' argument to mirt to save any future confusions.

COV frees a covariance term to be estimated between latent variables,
otherwise they are constrained to be orthgonal. The syntax says which
pairs should be freed. Also, if you are more comfortable with
so-called Q-matrix specification that also is available now.

The (f1*f1) syntax creates a product term in the latent variables, so
the following would be modelled if the syntax was for item 1

'F1= 1
(F1*F1) = 1'

logit(P_item1) = d + a1_F1 + a2_F1^2

Cheers.

Phil
